advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the excluded-paths test seed only *.md files under each EXCLUDED_PREFIX (e.g. infra/x.md, .github/workflows/x.md, tests/x.md) so the exclusion logic is genuinely exercised, or drop the non-.md prefixes as dead config.
evidence: tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py:103 'infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh': ... — a .sh file, never matched by SCOPED_GLOBS ('AGENTS.md', '.agents/rules/*.md', 'CONTRIBUTING.md', 'docs/**/*.md')
scripts/check_dco_identity.py:36-46 _scoped_files iterates SCOPED_GLOBS then applies EXCLUDED_PREFIXES; a non-.md file is dropped before the prefix filter ever runs
Exclusion only applied after a glob match: `for path in root.glob(pattern): ... if any(str(rel).startswith(prefix) for prefix in EXCLUDED_PREFIXES): continue` (check_dco_identity.py:39-44)
Only docs/** paths overlap the EXCLUDED_PREFIXES; infra/, .github/workflows/, tests/ can never be produced by any SCOPED_GLOB, so those three subjects in the test pass trivially
test asserts one combined `chk.find_violations(repo) == []` over all four seeded files (test_check_dco_identity.py:115)
advisory.finding: Three of the four files seeded in test_find_violations_ignores_excluded_automation_paths (.sh, .yml, .json) can never be selected by _scoped_files because SCOPED_GLOBS only match *.md — the test passes regardless of EXCLUDED_PREFIXES and gives false confidence that the infra/, .github/workflows/, and tests/ prefixes are functional. Only docs/experiments/ actually exercises the exclusion logic.
merged_from: test_find_violations_ignores_excluded_automation_paths does not actually exercise the exclusion filter for 3 of its 4 subjects: files under infra/, .github/workflows/, and tests/ can never match SCOPED_GLOBS (only AGENTS.md, .agents/rules/*.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/**/*.md are scanned), so they are never candidates and the exclusion check at check_dco_identity.py:43-44 never runs on them. Deleting the EXCLUDED_PREFIXES filter for those three prefixes would leave the test green. Only the docs/experiments/ subject genuinely exercises the exclusion path, and it is bundled into a single combined assertion so its regression signal is masked by the three no-op subjects.
scenarios: A future refactor removes '.github/workflows/' from EXCLUDED_PREFIXES — the test still passes green because the .yml was never in scope, masking the regression.
advisory.suggested_fix: Seed .md files under the excluded prefixes (infra/foo.md, tests/foo.md, etc.) so _scoped_files selects them and EXCLUDED_PREFIXES is the thing being tested; or reduce EXCLUDED_PREFIXES to ('docs/experiments/',) since only it can affect a *.md-only scan.

evidence: main() prints `f"{rel}:{line_no}: hardcoded DCO identity: {line.strip()}"` and a count summary to stderr (check_dco_identity.py:67-73)
Tests only assert `chk.main([...]) == 0` and `!= 0` (test_check_dco_identity.py:59,65); no capsys/stderr assertion exists
advisory.finding: The main() reporting path is only partially tested: tests assert main() exit codes (0 / nonzero) but never assert the stderr per-violation lines or the summary count message, so a regression in the violation-reporting output (wrong path/line rendering, missing count) would not be caught.
scenarios: A change to the stderr message format or a multi-violation count off-by-one would pass CI unnoticed.
